candidate.blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — medication administration and client education
candidate.blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — insulin administration
candidate.educational_objective: Teach the labeled meal timing for subcutaneous insulin lispro.

options.A: Administer it only at bedtime regardless of meal timing.
options.B: Administer it within 15 minutes before a meal or immediately after the meal.
options.C: Administer it routinely 30 to 60 minutes before the meal.
options.D: Administer it one hour after every meal.

candidate.rationale: Current HUMALOG (insulin lispro) labeling directs subcutaneous administration within 15 minutes before a meal or immediately after a meal. Its meal timing therefore differs from a regimen that requires a longer premeal interval. B is correct.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Subcutaneous insulin lispro should be administered within 15 minutes before a meal or immediately after a meal.
candidate.source_locator: Dosage and Administration, section 2.2 — Subcutaneous injection
candidate.source_version_date: Recent Major Changes: Dosage and Administration 01/2026
candidate.stem: A client is prescribed subcutaneous insulin lispro with meals. Which administration timing should the nurse teach?
